# Fanfarr v0.5.7

Fanfarr finds theme music for a Plex library, writes it beside the media as a
local `theme.mp3`, and keeps a permanent record of what it did and why.

## It runs on arm64 now

The image was amd64 only. It is a manifest list for `linux/amd64` and
`linux/arm64` under the same tag, and Docker pulls the one that matches the
host.

Each architecture is built on a runner of that architecture, not emulated.
ffmpeg is compiled from source in this image, and a from-source build under
emulation takes an hour or two instead of fifteen minutes -- so the arm64 image
would have been slow to build and slow to notice breaking.

Both are booted before they are published: the smoke test pulls the digest that
was just pushed, which on the arm64 runner is an arm64 image. It has been booted,
not assumed to work.

32-bit ARM is not built for. The Elixir base image publishes no such variant, and
Plex has largely left that hardware behind.

The first multi-arch build found three bugs, all of which are fixed here: the
Dockerfile fetched the x86_64 yt-dlp binary on every architecture, which on arm64
fails to execute; the digest artifacts could not be uploaded, because
`upload-artifact` rejects colons in paths and a digest is `sha256:...`; and the
merge job's tag list was built by a `sed` that prefixed nothing, so it published
no tags at all.

## Backups can be capped by size

A count is not a size. Seven snapshots of a library that keeps growing are not
seven snapshots of a fixed amount of disk, and the backup directory is on the
volume the database lives in -- the one that filling up breaks the app.

So there is a ceiling now: **Size cap (MB)** on the Backups card, or
`BACKUP_MAX_MB`. After each snapshot the oldest are deleted until the rest fit.

Three things it will not do, because they matter more than the ceiling does:

- **It never deletes the newest snapshot.**
- **It never deletes a pre-restore snapshot** -- that is the undo button for a
  restore you just made, and it has a cap of its own.
- **It never deletes, or counts, a file Fanfarr did not write.** Counting a
  database you copied in yourself would spend your snapshots to satisfy a total
  only that file breaks.

A ceiling smaller than a single snapshot is therefore exceeded rather than
obeyed. An empty backup directory is the one outcome worse than one that is too
big. It is off by default, so rotation behaves exactly as it did before until you
set it, and the card now shows what the snapshots cost against the cap.

## Fixed: three advisories in the HTTP client

`mint` 1.10.1 carried three advisories, one of them HIGH -- HPACK-indexed cookie
fields in HTTP/2 responses bypassing `max_header_list_size` and exhausting client
memory. mint is what Finch sits on, so it is what talks to Plex and to your
notification endpoint. All three are fixed in 1.10.2 and this ships 1.11.0.

Worth admitting how it was found: `mix hex.audit` had been failing in CI for
three runs while every local check passed, because `mix precommit` checked
dependencies but not their advisories. The audit is now part of `mix precommit`,
which is the actual fix -- a gate that reports green while CI is red is worse
than no gate.

## Smaller things

- **yt-dlp is pinned** to a release rather than `latest`, so the same commit
  builds the same image. `--build-arg YTDLP_VERSION=...` and mounting a newer
  binary over `/usr/local/bin/yt-dlp` both still work, and the System page
  reports the version it finds, so a pin that has gone stale is visible.
- **The notification card** says "Auto" and "Webhook Type" where it said "detect
  from the URL" and "Shape".
- **The CI actions moved off Node 20**: upload-artifact v7, download-artifact v8,
  cache v6.

## Upgrading

Pull the new image and restart; the database migrates itself on boot. Nothing
needs configuring:

- **Multi-arch**: nothing to do. Docker picks the right image for the host.
- **The size cap is off by default.** Rotation is unchanged until you set one.
- **The mint update is inside the image**, so pulling is the whole of it.
